The National Museum on Janpath holds one of the largest collections in India: Harappan seals and the bronze 'dancing girl', early historic and Buddhist sculpture, bronzes from south India and Mughal and Rajput paintings. An archaeologist takes your group through the galleries that matter most for your interests and shows you how to read an object: what it is made of, where it was found, and what it can and cannot tell us.

The gallery, date, pace and language are arranged to suit your group.

What it covers

  • The Harappan gallery: seals, weights, pottery and the bronze 'dancing girl'
  • Early historic and Buddhist sculpture, including the art of Gandhara
  • Bronzes from south India
  • Mughal and Rajput painting

How the time is spent

  1. Orientation 10 min

    How the museum is arranged, and the galleries chosen for your group.

  2. The Harappan gallery 35 min

    Seals, weights, ornaments and pottery from the Harappan cities, and what they show about trade, crafts and writing.

    You: read a seal and a weight: what was each one for?

  3. Sculpture 30 min

    Early historic and Buddhist sculpture, and how styles changed from region to region.

    You: compare two Buddha images and date them from their details

  4. Bronzes 25 min

    Bronze images from south India and how they were cast and carried in procession.

  5. Paintings 25 min

    Mughal and Rajput painting: who commissioned a painting, and what it was for.

    You: find the patron and the story in one painting

  6. Wrap-up 10 min

    Your questions, and what to see on a second visit.

Timings are a guide. The plan is confirmed with your quotation.

By the end you can

  • Read a museum object for its material, findspot, date and purpose.
  • Follow India's past from the Harappan cities to the Mughal court through the National Museum's collection.
  • Tell what an object shows from what a label or a later story adds to it.

You take away

A one-page trail of the objects you saw, with a reading list.
